comments.author: imglorp
comments.story: Lethal memory fail: Why drivers see, and then forget motorcyclists
comments.why: Illustrates the visibility problem and avoidance methods
comments.text: There's a second factor at work beyond memory - it's the human visual perceptive system. Bikes are not always moving across the visual field, and they aren't fitting the pattern of a bigger single-color smooth object so it's effectively camouflage. This is an outstanding vid on the whole subject illustrating the problem and some avoidance methods. This should be taught in rider training but it's not (US). [VIDEO]

comments.author: imglorp
comments.story: A Type of Road Junction that Kills Cyclists
comments.why: Explains perception psychology behind drivers failing to see motorcyclists
comments.text: This is also of high interest to motorcyclists who even have a name for the phenomena: SMIDSY (Sorry, Mate I Didn't See You). OP was focused on the A pillar and some other effects, while this excellent video goes a little further into some perception psychology about camouflage and how we perceive moving objects across backgrounds. You can ignore the motorcycle stuff but the explanation is enlightening. [VIDEO]

comments.author: IgorPartola
comments.story: A DIY E-bike Conversion on the Cheap
comments.why: Shows how little visible cyclists are despite high-viz gear
comments.text: Have you ever seen videos of how invisible you look despite all the high viz stuff? In some cases it becomes urban camo. Take a look at this video, especially at 2:30 or so. It’ll show you just how little visibility you’ll have: [VIDEO] Your best bet is to have all your clothing match your bike, Power Rangers style, to increase your chances. And lots and lots of very bright lights. One little handlebar mounted light is going to look like a reflection or a flashlight.
